overview:
First-term incumbent George Whitesides, a Democrat, defends a California district that leans Democratic by six points against Republican Jason Gibbs. Whitesides holds an overwhelming financial edge, having raised about $4.0 million with $2.6 million on hand, while Gibbs has raised roughly $380,000 with about $200,000 available. Outside groups have spent modestly to support the incumbent and almost nothing to oppose him.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the picture rests on fundamentals and market pricing. Prediction markets put Democratic chances near 93 percent. The district's lean, the incumbency advantage, and the money gap point to a Democratic margin in the low-to-mid teens, though the lack of polling confirmation keeps the seat short of the safest category. The district remains clearly favored to stay Democratic in November.
